fills.researcher_notes: One question per company — Kazakh-section operator = АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия», via its Uralsk branch (УМГ «Уральск»), not a Gazprom entity (the brief flags this pipeline specifically as one where the operator question genuinely splits by which side of the border a section sits on; per the already-settled note, do not re-litigate the 382 km Kazakh-section length). Three sources: (1) intergas.kz's 'General information' page — 'УМГ «Уральск»: МГ «Оренбург-Новопсков», МГ «Союз», МГ «Средняя Азия - Центр» с лупингами, МГ «Карачаганак-Уральск»'. (2) ecoportal.kz — Kazakhstan's public environmental-hearings portal, genuinely independent of the QazaqGaz/Intergas group — hosting a 2022 public hearing for permissible-emissions standards where the client/applicant is given as 'Филиал «УМГ «Уральск» АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия»' and the covered facility is explicitly '[магистральный] газопровод «Оренбург-Новопсков» с 170 км по 322 км' (170–322 km stretch) plus the 'Союз' trunk — i.e. Intergas Central Asia's Uralsk branch is the entity that filed for emissions permits on this exact line inside Kazakhstan (Syrym district, West Kazakhstan region). url_verifier 200s this page but substring-misses on it — it is JS-rendered, so I fetched and read it directly rather than treating the miss as a failure. (3) QazaqGaz's KASE-filed 2023 Integrated Annual Report lists 'МГ «Оренбург - Новопсков»' under 'АО «Интергаз Центральная Азия» осуществляет эксплуатацию следующих магистральных газопроводов' (p.21–22; PDF substring-check false negative, confirmed locally with pdftotext -layout). Marked tier=high/independent=true on the strength of source (2), a government hearings portal outside the QazaqGaz corporate family, corroborating sources (1) and (3).
